commands: sh -c 'find /usr/lib/security /usr/lib/methods -type f | while read file; do aclget "$file" 2>/dev/null | grep -e "[[:space:]]enabled$" >/dev/null 2>&1 && printf "%s\n" "$file"; done; printf "scan complete\n"'
blurb: This control verifies that no regular file under the system library directories /usr/lib/security and /usr/lib/methods carries an extended ACL (extended permissions enabled). The STIG inline script writes each aclget dump to a temp file and greps it for a whitespace-prefixed "enabled" line; this read-only port runs aclget to stdout and never writes a temp file. Any library file with an enabled extended ACL can grant principals beyond the intended base permissions access to security-critical library code, so any such file is a finding.
